Frederick stared at the glowing runes, the weight of eternity pressing against his mortal heart. The draft intensified, swirling the pages as if urging him toward a choice. He realized that immortality was not a gift, but a cage—a solitary existence watching the world decay while he remained unchanged. With a trembling hand, he did not reach for the vial of ingredients. Instead, he pulled a small, flint-covered torch from his belt. He struck it, the flame catching the dry parchment instantly. As the secret to eternal life burned away, turning to ash and smoke, Frederick felt a profound sense of peace. He had chosen mortality, and with it, the precious, fleeting beauty of a life that ends.

Christopher Columbus
